% Pattern: head/manual. A bold head names an item before its title, as
% "The Decomposition Theorem", "Smith's Lemma", "Cancelation axiom" in a list
% item, "Linearity Criterion" or "Geometric construction", and has no number.
% A bold group of words with no title is not a head. A case head writes a
% formula and a name in parentheses. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want head-1 statement/theorem -
% want head-2 statement/lemma -
% want head-3 statement/axiom -
% want head-4 statement/criterion -
% want head-5 definition/construction -
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-6 other/case -
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
Some text before.

\noindent {\bf The Covering Theorem}: Every compact space is bounded.

\noindent {\bf Smith's Lemma}: Every finite space is compact.

\noindent {\bf Bounded Spaces}: A space is bounded when a ball holds it.

\begin{itemize}
  \item {\bf Cancelation axiom.} Each map of spaces has an inverse.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Linearity Criterion:} A map is affine when its second derivative is zero.

\paragraph{\bf Geometric construction.}
Glue the opposite sides of a square.

\begin{theorem} Every closed ball is compact. \end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\textbf{Case $r<1$ (Small ball).} The ball lies in the unit ball.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
